title: tessera.audit-batches/1
description: What `tessera audit batch` writes to `<out-dir>/batches.json`, and prints with `--json` (RFC-0016 'Batching', RFC-0071 'The statement and the batching'): a sample's selected requests packed into proof batches by slot class `c = ⌈log2 max(L, 1)⌉` (decreasing) and first-fit decreasing on `L`, counting `2^{c + ⌈log2 R⌉}` tokens against `max_batch_tokens`, each request with the lengths its statement carries, read from the period's log and the previous period's. With --plan, oversized runtime advice layouts are split with the same packing rule; use the proving plan to reproduce prove --sample batch indices. Without a plan only the policy token bound is applied. Greedy only: every request is in one group until RFC-0061's pins are implemented. Informational: `tessera prove --sample` reads the batches from the sample and the logs again, never from this report.

manifest_digest.description: The period's manifest identity (RFC-0060), the sample's and every batch statement's `manifest_digest`, as lowercase hex.

sample.description: The sample seed (RFC-0016 'Sample derivation', step 3), as lowercase hex.

min_batch_tokens.description: The policy's `min_batch_tokens`: at most one batch of each slot class in a group has fewer counted tokens.

max_batch_tokens.description: The policy's `max_batch_tokens`: no batch has more counted tokens (`2^{c + ⌈log2 R⌉}`) except a request of class `c > ⌊log2 max_batch_tokens⌋`, alone.

selected.description: The sample's selected requests, each in exactly one batch.

index.description: The batch's position, from 0, which `tessera prove --batch` takes: groups in order, classes in decreasing order within each group, and each class's batches in the order they were opened.

group.description: The group the batch was packed in. Every request is greedy until RFC-0061's pins give temperature requests groups of their own.

requests.description: The batch's requests, in `RequestKey` order, as its statement lists them.

session_id.description: The request's session, as 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits: also the name of its stored transcript, `<session_id>.tst`.

tokens.description: `L`, the tokens of all its frames in the window (RFC-0063); 18446744073709551615 when a frame's length has no token count.

prompt_len.description: The tokens of its `In` frames in the window, its statement's `prompt_len`. Absent, with `output_len`, when a frame has no token count or a count is past 2^32 − 1: no statement can carry the request, and `tessera prove` refuses it with `ERR-WITNESS-ANCHOR`.

output_len.description: The tokens of its `Out` frames in the window, its statement's `output_len`.
